label: Kaymak
note: Balkan kajmak is salted and lightly soured

about.text: Kaymak, also known as qishta or sarshir, is a creamy dairy food similar to clotted cream, made from the milk of water buffalo, cows, sheep, or goats in Central Asia, most Turkic regions on the Eurasian Steppe, the Caucasus, Turkey, most Balkan countries, the Levant, Iran and Iraq.

how.text: Kaymak is made by heating milk slowly and long, so that the cream gathers into a skin that is lifted off. The Balkan kind may sour slightly while it stands; qishta is not soured.

facts.v: Milk held around 60 °C in wide shallow pans for several hours until the proteins coagulate and trap the fat into a layer; no culture and no coagulant (Wikipedia)
